Declared in .changeset/typed-subsumption.md.

`StoreRuntime` is the `@internal`, symbol-keyed store runtime port documented as absent from the public `Store` contract; it is not exported from any entrypoint, so no external consumer can name or author one. the query builder's subclass-expansion axis moves from a boolean `includeSubClasses` to a resolved `AliasExpansionAxis`, so the builder's internal state carries `startExpansion` / `expansion` and its config carries the store-level `defaultExpansion`, and a supertype alias resolves to `PolymorphicNodeType`. Declared in .changeset/typed-subsumption.md.

`search()`'s `includeSubClasses?: boolean` is replaced by `expansion?: "exact" | "subclasses"`, the same option name and values the query builder states, so one vocabulary covers both. The default is unchanged (`"exact"` — the search facade is not polymorphic by default), and `includeSubClasses: true` becomes `expansion: "subclasses"`. Declared in .changeset/typed-subsumption.md under "Breaking changes".

the two booleans `includeSubClasses` / `includeNarrower` are replaced by one `expansion: "exact" | "subclasses" | "narrower"` option on `from()`/`to()`/`fromDynamic()`/`toDynamic()`, so an alias states exactly one expansion axis and can no longer name a contradiction. A caller passes `{ expansion: "exact" }` where it passed `{ includeSubClasses: false }` and `{ expansion: "subclasses" }` where it passed `{ includeSubClasses: true }`; omitting the argument, `{}` and an explicit `undefined` all still mean "take the store default". Declared in .changeset/typed-subsumption.md under "Breaking changes".

Declared in .changeset/typed-subsumption.md under "Breaking changes".

the two booleans `includeSubClasses` / `includeNarrower` are replaced by one `expansion: "exact" | "subclasses" | "narrower"` option on `from()`/`to()`/`fromDynamic()`/`toDynamic()`, so an alias states exactly one expansion axis and can no longer name a contradiction. Declared in .changeset/typed-subsumption.md under "Breaking changes".

`StoreRuntime` is the `@internal`, symbol-keyed store runtime port documented as absent from the public `Store` contract; it is not exported from any entrypoint, so no external consumer can name or author one. The checker reaches it contravariantly only because `Store<G>` itself appears in parameter position on public functions such as `applyMergePlan`, which over-approximates a hand-authored `Store`-shaped value.
